gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Aventon counts the bike's own weight in the Aventure 3's 400 lb limit. That leaves about 324 lb for rider and gear (400 − 76 lb listed bike weight), which is less than the Lectric XPeak2's 330 lb rider/payload limit, though ChatGPT and the rival pages present the Aventure 3 as the bigger hauler.
standout_why: bicyclingland.com (cited) gives the Aventure 3 as '400 lb' with no rack rating, and says brands mix rider-only and total limits without saying which applies to each bike. ebikepost.com's compare page lists 400 lb and no rack rating for any of the three bikes, and its own table and body text disagree on what Velotric's 505 lb covers. sledgeback.com publishes no rack ratings. ChatGPT's own answer called the Aventure 3 '400-lb total weight limit' against the XPeak's '330-lb total payload', which implies the Aventon carries about 70 lb more. None of these pages subtracts the bike's weight or gives the Aventure 3's 59 lb rack figure.
decides: Once all three limits are put on the same rider-plus-gear basis, the Aventure 3 drops from second-highest capacity to the lowest of the three (about 324 lb against the XPeak2's 330 lb), and its rack is rated lowest too (59 lb against 60 and 66). For a hunter whose own weight plus pack, stand and gear runs close to 300 lb, the Aventure 3 is no longer the 'more capacity' upgrade over the cheaper XPeak2. The Velotric Nomad 2 stays top for hauling either way: even if its 505 lb 'Max Bike Load' includes the bike, about 430 lb is left (505 − 75), and its rack is rated 66 lb.

findings.label: What the 400 lb limit covers
findings.value: 400 lb total, including rider, gear and the bike
findings.source_title: What holds up when you load an Aventure 3 for a multi-day trip (Aventon blog, 2026-10-08)
findings.note: Aventon's own wording: 'total payload' covers 'rider, gear, and bike combined'.

findings.label: Rider + gear capacity, normalised
findings.value: ≈324 lb (≈321 lb at the bike's measured weight)
findings.source_title: What holds up when you load an Aventure 3 for a multi-day trip (Aventon blog)
findings.note: 400 lb − 76 lb (Aventon's listed weight, same page) = 324 lb. Using OutdoorGearLab's measured 79 lb: 400 − 79 = 321 lb. The same blog says independent scales show 78–79 lb.

findings.label: Rear rack rating
findings.note: 'you can load up to 59 pounds on the included rear rack'. Aventon's blog gives the same 59 lb maximum.

findings.label: Measured range, hilly course
findings.value: 28.3 mi with over 1,300 ft of climbing
findings.note: Measured by OutdoorGearLab. Rider weight and assist level not stated. Aventon claims up to 65 mi.

findings.label: Rider weight / payload / rear rack
findings.value: 330 lb rider, 330 lb payload, 60 lb rear rack
findings.source_title: Lectric Help Center: What is the maximum rider weight?
findings.note: Lectric's table lists the rider and payload limits as the same 330 lb, so the bike's own 75 lb is not counted. Rider plus gear is therefore 330 lb, 6 lb more than the Aventure 3's normalised 324 lb.

findings.label: Load rating / rear rack / weight
findings.value: 505 lb max load; 66 lb rack; 82 lb measured (75 lb claimed)
findings.source_title: Electric Bike Review, Velotric Nomad 2 Review: A Plush Powerhouse (Mike East)
findings.note: Mike East's scale read 82 lb with the battery. Rider + gear is 505 lb if the rating excludes the bike, or 505 − 75 = 430 lb (505 − 82 = 423 lb measured) if it includes it. Either way it is the highest of the three.

findings.label: Measured range at full power
findings.value: 26 mi (Boost, PAS 5, full throttle); about 65 mi (Eco, PAS 3)
findings.source_title: Electric Bike Review, Velotric Nomad 2 review
findings.note: Electric Bike Review's tests, 705.6 Wh pack. The bullet list says 25 mi and 64 mi. Rider weight not stated.

findings.label: Max payload and bike weight
findings.value: 400 lb payload; 92 lb bike with battery
findings.source_title: Himiway blog: E-Bike Weight Limits Explained (2026-09-10)
findings.note: The page does not say whether the 400 lb includes the bike. It also notes that the 20-inch D5 2.0 listing shows 440 lb. If the bike is counted, the 400 lb rating leaves 400 − 92 = 308 lb for rider and gear. If not, it leaves 400 lb.
